messages:
jen: forwarding a customer's thread — they say invoice shows ~18k embedding units but dashboard shows 11k. Customer pasted request IDs and payload.

jen: sample payload they sent:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{ \"model\": \"text-embedding-003\", \"input\": [\"short text\", \"very long text...\"] }
```

samir: do we know if the invoice counts pairwise reranks vs per-input? sounds like per-pair accounting for rerank could double-count.

ingrid: billing logs show 1765901 request units for that account for date 2026-01-12, matches invoice. Dashboard query used aggregated 'embedding_units' metric, might have filtered out failed attempts.

maya: also saw earlier bug where batched embeddings with heterogeneous lengths were padded to max_len before dimensioning, which increments batched token accounting — could explain delta.

samir: can customer share one request_id from the invoice? also need raw request payload and whether they used rerank endpoint or embeddings+rerank client logic.

jen: they provided req id: req_01GfX... attached. They confirm using our /v1/embeddings endpoint with batches of 256 inputs, some >1024 chars. They said they pre-trim inputs client-side but still seeing mismatch.

samir: pulled logs for req_01GfX: server accepted batch size 256, truncated at 2048 tokens per input, logged token_count=51200, billed_unit_calc=51200 — dashboard query excludes truncation overflow records by default. suspect truncation-to-max-token leads to higher billed tokens than dashboard shows.

maya: note: earlier change in batching kernel added pad-to-power-of-two behavior for speed on XPU, which pads sequences to 128/256 boundaries. That padding is included in our internal token accounting and therefore invoice; dashboard metrics pipeline removes padding to show 'effective' tokens. discrepancy source.

ingrid: ok makes sense. action: need to (1) give customer explanation, (2) adjust dashboard ETL to surface both 'raw_billed_tokens' and 'effective_tokens', (3) open billing review to consider credit if sudden spike.

billing-bot: created ticket BILL-2026-382 with summary \"Invoice spike due to padding/truncation in batched embeddings\" link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/BILL-2026-382

samir: repro steps for eng if needed:
```
# reproduce locally against staging
curl -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings \
 -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TEST\" \
 -d '{\"model\":\"text-embedding-003\",\"input\": ["A"*1000, "B"*1000]}'
```

maya: creating a small script to compare billed vs effective tokens and run on customer's payloads, will attach results to the ticket.

jen: customer ok with investigation, asked for interim guidance — what to tell them?

ingrid: explain padding/truncation difference, offer to run their payload through staging script and surface per-request breakdown; offer provisional credit if spike is >50% and occurred within one billing period.

samir: assigning to eng-runtime to verify pad-to-power-of-two commit and assess if we can avoid counting pad in billing pipeline without perf hit.

jen: thanks team, I'll send customer an initial write-up and reference to BILL-2026-382.
